title: How to Use External APIs in Business Central
summary: This post explains how to consume external APIs from within Business Central by making HTTP requests using the HttpClient data type and parsing JSON responses. It includes two practical examples: retrieving Chuck Norris jokes and validating email addresses through public APIs, with complete AL code samples and guidance on security prompts.
key_points: APIs provide an interface to access services and data from outside Business Central using HTTP requests with GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, or PATCH methods
The HttpClient data type is used to send HTTP requests, set headers, and handle responses containing JSON data
JSON responses must be parsed using JsonObject to extract specific fields needed for your business logic
Public APIs can be found through search engines or in service documentation, with resources like GitHub's public-apis list available
Business Central shows a security prompt when extensions attempt to access external services to prevent unauthorized data exfiltration

quotes.text: An interface that we can use to allow our application to access some service through programming.
quotes.why_it_matters: This is the fundamental definition of an API that guides developers in understanding how Business Central can interact with external systems.
